issue_context.title: Philips Hue "lights" attribute not useful in current state
issue_context.body:
At present, Hue "Rooms" feature an attribute that lists all the lights within the room. However, this attribute isn't particularly practical for Home Assistant because it provides "Friendly Names" instead of entity_ids. Moreover, as far as I'm aware, there is no straightforward method for cross-referencing the entity_id from the friendly name, especially considering that friendly names are not guaranteed to be unique. It would be a valuable enhancement if we could obtain a list of the entities associated with this particular "group."

What we currently get:
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/518673/219dddc6-5ce9-4e41-a709-ff554249de13)


What would make it more useful:
![image (1)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/518673/5a60b0e9-8296-418a-b4ea-9ec90d284911)

as @tdejneka stated this is for reporting bugs, not feature requests.
What would be the benefit of having the entity ids as attribute ? Also, its not guaranteed that all lights of the group are visible/available within HA.

First of all, I apologize for any confusion caused by my initial approach. Moving forward, I'll make sure to utilize the forums for better engagement. I think there are a several compelling reasons why this makes sense: 1. **Enhanced Consistency in Configuration:** When you define a group of lights in `lights.yaml` like so: ``` - platform: group name: Kitchen Overhead Hues unique_id: 9DAEDFD3-0E4E-4235-8AAB-2128A2C56415 entities: - light.kitchen_overhead_hue_1 - light.kitchen_overhead_hue_2 - light.kitchen_overhead_hue_3 - light.kitchen_overhead_hue_4 - light.kitchen_overhead_hue_5 ``` The attributes of this group would provide access to the individual light entities. This uniform approach brings consistency to the handling of light groups created within Home Assistant as opposed to directly in the Hue app. . By comparison, here is what one created in the Hue App is like: This consistency fosters coherence between the two distinct methods of creating "light groups." 2. **Synchronized Light Control:** Creating the group (zone/room) within the Hue app, rather than in Home Assistant, offers tangible benefits. When a light is toggled on, off, or adjusted through an HA service, HA-managed group lights might exhibit a slight delay between individual light reactions. Conversely, a group established within the Hue app triggers simultaneous changes across all included lights, resulting in a more natural and seamless experience. 3. **Multiple Applications for Entity Lists:** The list of entities generated from this feature holds significant utility across various use cases: - Tha HACS [Hue Like Card ](https://github.com/Gh61/lovelace-hue-like-light-card) from HACS brings a user-friendly Hue app-like interface to Home Assistant. It can replicate the color display of each sub-light in a rainbow fashion similar to the Hue app. With this enhancement, the setup process could be streamlined, offering a seamless experience. - For users with [Inovelli light switches](https://inovelli.com/collections/inovelli-blue-series) which feature customizable light bars, automations can be created to synchronize the light bar colors with the corresponding Hue lights in the controlled group. This eliminates the need for a redundant light group in HA and simplifies adjustments. - It also facilitates dynamic interactions with template sensors. For example, you can iterate through sub-lights and gather details for other template sensors, as demonstrated in the code snippet below: ``` - name: Current Lights On state: >- {% set ns = namespace(count=0) %} {% for light in state_attr('light.all_lights', 'entity_id') %} {% set ns.count = ns.count + (1 if has_value(light) and is_state(light, 'on') else 0) %} {% endfor %} {{ ns.count }} ``` 4. **Mitigating Entity Visibility Concerns:** Addressing concerns about entity visibility, it's worth noting that, by default, all entities within the Hue integration are enabled and shared. While entities can be disabled, this applies equally to conventional light groups, resulting in a comparable behavior. Users can easily check the current status of an entity ID's visibility in their code. All in all, there's a multitude of compelling arguments supporting the integration of this feature into the Hue ecosystem. These advantages range from consistency in configuration to improved user experience and broader application possibilities. I believe that adding this functionality would greatly enhance the Hue integration within Home Assistant.

I will look into this later this week but if I remember it correctly there was a reason I did not fill the entities attribute because the underlying entities of a Hue group were not known in the group light. I'll check if we can make this easiliy happen without any hacks or impact to performance.
I appreciate it! Let me know if there's any other info I can provide
